title: Eye catchers
slide_intent: Teach designers to establish one dominant reading distance for a poster, banner or flyer. Secondary information can sit at a much smaller scale once the main message attracts attention.
strategic_value: Frontline AIDS can carry short campaign language across large banners and small handouts while retaining the order of message and action.
demonstration: Three annotated formats compare a pink poster, a small flyer and a tall pull-up banner. Large boxed headlines dominate, with details and contact information in smaller roles.
practical_value: Identify the message someone should read from a distance and the action they can read up close. Check that the hierarchy still works when format changes.

content_islands.name: Scale guidance
content_islands.spec: Use the left paragraph to explain where high-impact formats can use dramatic changes in type scale.

content_islands.name: Poster and flyer
content_islands.spec: Place the poster high in the field and the paired small-format flyer views along the lower left. Label the main heading, subhead and supporting roles.

content_islands.name: Pull-up banner
content_islands.spec: Set the vertical banner at right. Preserve the large headline near the top, photograph and lower call to action. Use surrounding notes to identify each typographic setting.
